reasoning: A talk that teaches a tool.
bigIdea: Measure a command until its numbers settle, and compare it against a reference, never once by hand.

beats.name: Orientation: What we’ll learn and why it matters
beats.claim: A benchmark you run once tells you nothing; hyperfine runs it until the numbers settle.

beats.name: Foundations: Core concepts and terminology
beats.claim: Hyperfine runs every command at least 10 times and aims for about 3 seconds of measurement.

beats.name: Application: Worked examples
beats.claim: Warmup runs and prepare commands decide whether you measure a warm cache or a cold one.

beats.name: Mastery: Edge cases and pitfalls
beats.claim: Below 5 ms, a shell's startup is more noise than your command: run it without one.

beats.name: Assessment: Quick checks for understanding
beats.claim: In hyperfine's own example, fd finds the files 9.8x faster than find.

beats.name: Transfer: How to apply in the real world
beats.claim: Compare your branches with a parameter list and a setup command, not by hand.
